subject: Post-call: vendor gap matrix, test plan, and next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Thomas <ben.thomas@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: vendor gap matrix, test plan, and next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today, Ben — good conversation and clear priorities. Quick recap from our call and proposed path forward so we all have the same checklist.

Top problems you called out
- High token/service spend for real-time support flows (esp. peak hours).
- Hard latency tail for short-turn chat (SLO target: p95 < 200ms).
- Compliance: data residency, audit logs, and ability to run in your VPC for regulated customers.

Goals you shared
- Replace current hosted endpoint with a vendor that can meet p95 latency under 200ms at peak QPS and reduce per-message cost by ~25%.
- Start with a narrow pilot (support channel) and expand to policy-automation if pilot succeeds.
- Complete security validation and procurement within 8 weeks.

Decision criteria (what I heard)
1) Security & compliance (SOC2 + VPC/private deployment capability)
2) Latency & reliability under realistic load
3) Unit economics (tokens + infra)
4) Integration effort & SDK maturity

Competitive snapshot from today's discussion
- Vendor A: strong latency under load but limited private deployment options (needs more gating for your compliance team).
- Vendor B: cost-competitive but current throughput limits at long contexts; may require model sharding.
- Redwood: unified hosted + private options, runtime-level batching, and per-request audit logs — initial benchmarks look promising but we need a run under your workloads.

Recommended next steps (timeline estimate)
- This week: sign off on the attached test plan CSV (Fintech test matrix) and confirm the three representative prompts/flows you want in the pilot. (Owner: Fintech / Due: Thu 9/16)
- Next week: kickoff performance tests (Marissa will run the baseline/compare scripts against our hosted and dedicated stacks). (Owner: Redwood / Target: 9/21–9/23)
- Week after: security questionnaire/desk review with your security team and provide VPC deployment checklist. (Owner: Redwood + Fintech / Target: 10/1)

Attachments: redwood-onepager-q3.pdf (brief), fintech-test-plan-20260914.csv (test matrix). Also included a simple load script we can iterate on.

Open questions to lock down before test kickoff
- Which 3 user flows should we prioritize (support-short, support-long, policy-automation)?
- Do you require HSM/KMS integration for the pilot or is RBAC/audit logs sufficient for initial testing?
- Any IP/masking rules we should bake into the test generator?

If that matches your memory, I can update the test plan with the flows you pick and we’ll put firm slots on the calendar. Thanks — looking forward to progressing.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

---
Attachments referenced: redwood-onepager-q3.pdf (1 page), fintech-test-plan-20260914.csv (test matrix), load-script.sh (bash)
From: Ben Thomas <ben.thomas@fintechco.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Paul Kim <paul.kim@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: vendor gap matrix, test plan, and next steps

Thanks Grace — that recap is spot on. A few clarifications and our prioritization:

Priorities (in order)
1) Compliance (must be able to meet our data residency and provide per-request audit logs)
2) Latency (p95 < 200ms for short chat flows)
3) Cost (target ~25% savings is ideal but secondary to the two above)

On the open questions:
- Flows: let's prioritize support-short (short context support chat), support-long (longer multi-turn troubleshooting), and a simple policy-automation prompt (small batch).
- KMS: for the pilot, audit logs + RBAC are acceptable; KMS/HSM will be required for production and we need a design doc for that during the security review.
- Masking rules: yes — strip account IDs and SSNs from generated test data; we will provide a small sanitizer script.

I've added Paul (procurement) to keep timelines visible — Paul, we'll loop you in on the SOW/procurement once we have the test results.

I'll review the attached CSV and confirm flows by EOD Thursday 9/16. Thanks to Marissa and Aditya for joining the call.

—Ben
Ben Thomas
Head of Product, Conversational Support | FintechCo
ben.thomas@fintechco.com | +1 212-555-0110

Subject: Re: Post-call: vendor gap matrix, test plan, and next steps

Great — thanks Ben. I pulled together a proposed test matrix based on the flows you confirmed. Summary below and I attached a CSV and a tiny load script for the baseline.

Planned tests- Short-chat throughput: sustained 200 QPS, 1k concurrent users, measure p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate.
- Long-chat context: mixed sequence lengths up to 2k tokens, backpressure behavior and memory/KV cache utilization.
- Batch policy automation: 500 concurrent batch requests, token cost measurement and tail latency.

What we'll deliver after tests- Side-by-side CSV with metrics across Vendor A, Vendor B, and Redwood (hosted + dedicated).
- Sample logs and audit entries demonstrating per-request metadata and retention windows.
- Cost model: tokens + infra to estimate per-message economics at your scale.

Small notes/asks- Can you share the 3 representative prompt templates (or allow us to use the ones in the attached CSV)?
- Confirm whether test traffic should originate from your VPC or if we should run the hosted baseline from our us-west region.

Schedule proposal
- Baseline runs (hosted Redwood): 9/21–9/22
- Dedicated baseline + Vendor A/B: 9/23–9/25
- Results review and walkthrough: 9/28 (30–45 min)

Attachments: fintech-test-plan-20260914.csv, load-script.sh

If those dates work I'll block time and share calendar invites.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
